Markus / Soojin — quick clarifications from the infra side for the cover note: 

1) Replication: Production workloads are placed primarily in us-west-2 (single-primary) with asynchronous cross-region replication to us-east-1 for disaster recovery. We do not perform synchronous cross-region writes for low-latency inference; the DR replica is cold-warmed for rapid failover.

2) KMS: For hosted accounts we use Redwood-managed KMS keys (AWS KMS) with key rotation and IAM controls. For Private (VPC) customers we support customer-managed KMS keys and can provide key ARNs in NDA workflows.

3) Operator identities: we can provide the non-human operator roster (agent IDs and owner teams) in the spreadsheet. Full human-readable names may be redacted in the public RFI spreadsheet; legal will process name disclosures under the standard mutual NDA / DPA.

I'll propose the following sentence for the cover note: "Redwood maintains a documented subprocessor roster and a formal change-notice process. For hosted customers, production infrastructure is hosted in AWS us-west-2 with asynchronous failover to us-east-1; encryption at rest is provided via AWS KMS with options for customer-managed keys in Private deployments. Operator identities may be redacted in public materials and disclosed under NDA."

If that text looks good I'll drop it into the cloud_assurance_matrix.pdf and push a v2 of the roster spreadsheet.
